questions.q: What does the Assignment element actually do?
options: It permanently deletes a variable
It sets the value of a variable in memory — it does not save anything to Salesforce by itself
It saves a record directly to the database
It queries Salesforce for matching records
questions.explain: Assignment only changes what a variable holds in memory; a separate Create or Update Records element is needed to save that to Salesforce.

questions.q: What are the three parts of every Assignment element row?
options: Object, Field, Filter
Label, Description, API Name
Variable, Operator, Value
Source, Target, Formula
questions.explain: Every Assignment row specifies a Variable to change, an Operator controlling how, and a Value to use.

questions.q: In the 'Set New Opportunity Values' example, what does the fifth row (Variable: NewOpportunities, Operator: Add, Value: NewOpportunity) actually do?
options: It deletes the NewOpportunity record
It appends the NewOpportunity record onto the NewOpportunities collection
It replaces the entire NewOpportunities collection with a single record
It creates a new Opportunity object definition
questions.explain: The Add operator appends a value — here, a record — onto a collection variable rather than replacing it.

questions.q: In the shipping-address flow example (Decision branching into two Assignment elements, both feeding one Update Account element), why do both Assignment elements feed the same Update Records element instead of each having their own?
options: Flow Builder requires exactly one Update Records element per flow
Whichever branch runs, the same record variable ends up holding the right value in memory — one Update Records element then commits it, regardless of which path was taken
Update Records elements cannot be used inside Decision branches
It's required purely for canvas layout reasons, not functional ones
questions.explain: Both Assignment elements write into the same record variable; a single Update Records element after the merge commits whichever value was set.

questions.q: An Assignment element sets a record variable's Status field to 'Closed,' but no Update Records or Create Records element runs afterward. What happens to that record in Salesforce?
options: It's automatically saved as soon as the Assignment element finishes
Nothing — the change exists only in memory and is never written to Salesforce
Salesforce saves it at the end of the flow automatically, regardless of other elements
The flow throws an error immediately
questions.explain: Without a data element like Update Records to commit it, the Assignment's change to the record variable never reaches the actual Salesforce record.
